primary_topics: Last official meeting of CJP as Chief Justice with the bench and bar of Cebu -- testimonial dinner, November 24, 2006 (the same day as the CA Cebu marker-laying and the Lapu-lapu electronic court topping); two weeks before his mandatory retirement

Cebu's unique relationship with the judiciary: three of 21 Chief Justices (Pedro Yap, Marcelo Fernan, Hilario Davide); considerable APJR pilot-testing attention; CA Cebu building, electronic court of Lapu-lapu, Halls of Justice
Antonio Oposa's environmental advocacy as Cebu's contribution to Philippine jurisprudence
Liberty and prosperity as the governing philosophy exported to the Global Forum (October 2006); the bench and bar of Cebu as always in the forefront of the quest
sub_topics: Context: 'In just two weeks, I shall be retiring from the judiciary. This testimonial dinner is therefore especially meaningful, because it is my last official meeting, as Chief Justice, with the members of the bench and bar of Cebu.'

Same-day events: 'I would like to cite the establishment of a Court of Appeals branch in Cebu City, for which we laid the building marker this morning; the model electronic court of Lapu-lapu, whose building was topped off also this morning; and the establishment of various Halls of Justice in the province in the past few years.'

Cebu's three CJs: Pedro Yap, Marcelo B. Fernan, and Hilario G. Davide Jr. -- three of the 21 Chief Justices in the Philippine judiciary's 105-year history; Pampanga: 18 justices but only two CJs (Jose Abad Santos and Panganiban)

Antonio Oposa: 'distinguished environmentalist' whose 'pioneering efforts to preserve and conserve our environment have made all of us realize that our generation owes the next and succeeding generations the responsibility of maintaining nature's rhythmic balance'

Liberty and prosperity: 'twin beacons for the Philippine judiciary'; Global Forum held last October in Makati City; 'most if not all of the judiciaries represented accepted them as worthy of adoption'

Closing: 'that hope springs eternal because of the realization that the bench and bar of Cebu would always be in the forefront of our collective quest for liberty and prosperity under the rule of law'

stances.claim: Cebu's disproportionate contribution to the Philippine judiciary -- three of 21 Chief Justices -- is the governing justification for why Cebu has received disproportionate APJR attention and resources. The pattern of justice is reciprocal: Cebu has given the judiciary its leaders; the judiciary has given Cebu its institutions.

notable_anecdotes: Three CJs from Cebu, two from Pampanga: Cebu produced Pedro Yap, Marcelo Fernan and Hilario Davide -- three of 21 CJs in 105 years. Pampanga, home of 18 justices, produced only two CJs: Jose Abad Santos and CJP himself.

Three institutional milestones in one day: the CA Cebu building marker, the Lapu-lapu electronic court topping, and the bench-and-bar testimonial dinner all happened on November 24, 2006 -- the same day as SD140.

The Global Forum reception: 'The twin Liberty and Prosperity beacons have been exported by our Supreme Court during the Global Forum on Liberty and Prosperity held last October in Makati City. Equally important, most if not all of the judiciaries represented accepted them as worthy of adoption.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered November 24, 2006 as CJP's final official engagement with the Cebu bench and bar -- a testimonial dinner held on the same day as the CA Cebu building marker-laying (SD140) and the Lapu-lapu electronic court topping -- this address opens: 'In just two weeks, I shall be retiring from the judiciary. This testimonial dinner is therefore especially meaningful, because it is my last official meeting, as Chief Justice, with the members of the bench and bar of Cebu.' He notes the day's three institutional milestones (CA Cebu building, Lapu-lapu electronic court, Halls of Justice) as products of the APJR's special attention to Cebu. The justification: 'Cebu has produced and nurtured three of the 21 Chief Justices in the Philippine judiciary's 105-year history: Chief Justices Pedro Yap, Marcelo B. Fernan, and Hilario G. Davide Jr.' (Pampanga, by comparison, has 18 justices but only two CJs -- Jose Abad Santos and CJP himself.) He praises Antonio Oposa: 'his pioneering efforts to preserve and conserve our environment have made all of us realize that our generation owes the next and succeeding generations the responsibility of maintaining nature's rhythmic balance.' On the Global Forum (October 2006): 'The twin Liberty and Prosperity beacons have been exported by our Supreme Court... most if not all of the judiciaries represented accepted them as worthy of adoption.' Close: 'that hope springs eternal because of the realization that the bench and bar of Cebu would always be in the forefront of our collective quest for liberty and prosperity under the rule of law. Daghang salamat! Maayong gabi-i kaninyong tanan!'
